claims.text: Tungsten carbide can serve as an effective catalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction.
Tungsten carbide can serve as an effective catalyst for the hydrogen oxidation reaction.
Tungsten carbide has enhanced durability compared with conventional noble-metal catalysts.
A clean, well-defined WC surface exposes catalytically active sites.
WC can be deployed as a catalyst electrode for HER and HOR in acidic electrolyte.
WC may be used for HER and HOR in alkaline electrolyte if appropriately adapted.
The carbide bonding network and tungsten d-band electronic structure mediate WC catalytic behavior.
The electronic structure of tungsten carbide emulates some catalytic properties of platinum-group metals.
WC binds adsorbed hydrogen with an optimal strength for efficient HER turnover.
WC binds adsorbed hydrogen with an optimal strength for efficient HOR turnover.
The robust carbide structure of WC increases resistance to corrosion during prolonged electrochemical cycling.
The robust carbide structure of WC increases resistance to structural degradation during prolonged electrochemical cycling.
A WC-based electrode will deliver lower HER overpotentials than conventional Pt-based catalysts under identical conditions.
A WC-based electrode will deliver lower HOR overpotentials than conventional Pt-based catalysts under identical conditions.
A WC-based electrode will maintain high HER and HOR turnover frequencies over extended operation.
WC durability will be comparable or superior to that of conventional Pt-based catalysts under identical conditions.
WC catalytic performance may vary with synthesis method, particle size, pH, and temperature.
Tungsten-based materials are considered for applications involving harsh operating conditions.
Direct evidence for enhanced WC HER/HOR activity and long-term durability in real electrolytic environments is limited.
